$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.query.merge. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-KEYED-MERGE-THEIRS-LOST
arms.find: if (old != null && old.text == mine.text) return other.text;
arms.replace: if (old != null && old.text == mine.text) return mine.text;
arms.note: a child only theirs changed keeps our unchanged text, so the merge driver drops the other branch's change without a conflict

arms.name: M-KEYED-MERGE-APPEND-ORDER
arms.note: a child theirs added lands before the one ours added at the same place, so the merged order depends on which side merged into which

arms.name: M-KEYED-MERGE-NO-RECURSION
arms.find: if (oldTree != null && mineTree != null && otherTree != null)
arms.replace: if (oldTree != null && mineTree != null && otherTree != null && false)
arms.note: a type both sides changed is a conflict as a whole instead of being merged member by member, so two members added beside each other stop merging

arms.name: M-DECLARATION-TREE-SPACING-IS-CONTENT
arms.note: the blank line a member gains when ours inserts one above it reads as a change of that member, so theirs' edit of it becomes a conflict

arms.name: M-KEYED-MERGE-NO-PLACE-LINE-MERGE
arms.note: a body both sides edited on different lines becomes a conflict although git's line merge of that one place is clean

arms.name: M-DECLARATION-TREE-CONDITIONAL-BLIND
arms.note: a member added inside an #if region is merged by key and can land past its #end, silently unconditional

arms.name: M-KEYED-MERGE-REPLACEMENTS-UNITED
arms.note: two different renames of one member, or two replacements of one list value, are both kept instead of conflicting

arms.name: M-KEYED-MERGE-RENAME-AGAINST-DELETE
arms.note: a member one side renamed and the other deleted comes back under its new name, silently, because by key a rename is a removal and an addition
